messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (faithfulness) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is every claim in the brief supported by the cited evidence and the fact sheet, with nothing overstated and no cited contrary evidence left out? Pass means yes.
Fail on an uncited claim, a number that is off the fact sheet, a scope wider than the cited accounts, a paraphrase placed in quotation marks, or an ignored contrary citation.
The evidence is the brief, the cited insights and the fact sheet (accounts, ARR, mentions, routes, renewals).
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "brief": "## Problem\nUsers cannot align claim references generated by Keelwater software with their internal naming conventions. This causes mismatches when pulling reports or syncing with external suppliers, disrupting workflow accuracy and forcing manual corrections.\n\n## Who is affected\n- The issue was raised during the onboarding process by Cindermill Trade Cover [i:213e04100f910bef].\n\n## Evidence\n- The problem was mentioned 1 time in total [i:213e04100f910bef].\n- The mention occurred specifically via the onboarding route [i:213e04100f910bef].\n- The customer, Cindermill Trade Cover, stated, \"First, we need to set up a custom claim-reference format — our internal systems rely on specific prefixes and sequences. We really need to set up a custom claim-reference format because our internal systems use specific naming conventions and we can’t have mismatches when pulling reports or syncing with suppliers.\" [i:213e04100f910bef].\n- This issue is currently associated with 1 account [i:213e04100f910bef].\n- The total Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) associated with the accounts mentioning this issue is £210,000.0 [i:213e04100f910bef].\n\n## Why now\n- The feedback was provided on 2026-10-12 [i:213e04100f910bef].\n- Cindermill Trade Cover, with an ARR of £210,000.0, has a renewal date of 2027-04-03 [i:213e04100f910bef].\n- There have been 0 renewals in the last 90 days [i:213e04100f910bef].",
 "cited_insights": [
  {
   "id": "213e04100f910bef",
   "quote": "First, we need to set up a custom claim-reference format — our internal systems rely on specific prefixes and sequences. We really need to set up a custom claim-reference format because our internal systems use specific naming conventions and we can’t have mismatches when pulling reports or syncing with suppliers.",
   "account": "Cindermill Trade Cover",
   "route": "onboarding",
   "date": "2026-10-12T08:59:00+00:00"
  }
 ],
 "fact_sheet": {
  "as_of": "2026-11-03",
  "accounts_n": 1,
  "mentions_n": 1,
  "routes_n": 1,
  "mentions_by_route": {
   "onboarding": 1
  },
  "arr_total_gbp": 210000.0,
  "renewals_90d_n": 0,
  "accounts": [
   {
    "name": "Cindermill Trade Cover",
    "arr_gbp": 210000.0,
    "renewal_date": "2027-04-03",
    "mentions": 1
   }
  ]
 }
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "I checked every claim in the brief against the cited insight and fact sheet. The mention count (1), route (onboarding), account count (1), ARR (£210,000.0), date (2026-10-12), renewal date (2027-04-03), and 0 renewals in 90 days all match the fact sheet, and the direct quotation matches the insight's quote verbatim with no paraphrase in quotation marks. The problem description's scope (one account, one mention) is not overstated, and no contrary evidence exists.", "verdict": "pass"}
